findings.text: Migrate isolation admits only LRU resident folios and rejects pinned anonymous pages via a racy refcount versus mapcount test, rejects file backed pages when the request lacks filesystem scope, rejects unevictable folios unless unevictable mode is set, and rejects writeback or dirty folios in async mode unless they lack a mapping or the mapping offers nonblocking migration and is accessible.

Successful isolation clears LRU membership under protection, removes the folio from its LRU vector, accounts isolated pages by anonymous versus file class, appends to the migrate list, and stops the block scan once the cluster limit is reached unless finishing the whole block or contended.

Isolation uses success, fail with putback, fail with skip advance, abort, and out of memory exits: failures can release already isolated pages, jump the scan cursor to the next skip point, and only update cached scanner state when the block end is reached with either no isolation or finish block set.

The migrate scanner drops any held LRU vector lock before movable operations isolation and before dropping a folio reference, reacquires the owning vector lock when the folio belongs to a different vector, marks skip state under that lock, and always releases the lock on abort and at scan end.

A short folio trylock is used only on the dirty async or unevictable mapped path to recheck the current mapping, migration support, and accessibility, then unlocked before LRU flag manipulation; failure to acquire abandons that folio.

Buddy order is read without the zone lock as an unsafe hint that may only cause skipping a usable block, folio order based skipping is checked under the vector lock, and folio mapping is revalidated under folio lock to close a race with truncation.

Range isolation walks a pfn interval block by block, clamps the first block to the zone start and each block end to the requested end, skips blocks with no valid pages, forces unevictableinclusive mode, and stops on first error or when the cluster target is reached.

A source block is rejected when persistently marked skip; background compaction accepts all remaining blocks; direct compaction rejects CMA blocks for non CMA requests, accepts all blocks in synchronous mode, and in async mode restricts movable or whole block requests to movable blocks and other requests to matching migratetype.

A target block is rejected when it contains a sufficiently large buddy free page, accepted unconditionally when block suitability checks are ignored, otherwise accepted only when its migratetype is movable or CMA.
The freelist scan budget starts from the compaction cluster size shifted down by accumulated fast search failures, with a lower bound guaranteeing at least a minimal scan.
The two scanners are considered met when the free scanner pageblock index is at or below the migrate scanner pageblock index.
Freelist rotation moves either the segment before a free page or the segment ending at it to the list tail, leaving the list unchanged when the page is already at the corresponding edge.

Isolation around a pfn does nothing when free pages already cover migrate pages or during direct async compaction; otherwise it isolates free pages in the containing zone clamped pageblock and marks the block to skip when the block was fully consumed.

Order search walks downward and wraps from below zero to one below the requested order; completing a full cycle decrements the stored search order with wrap and signals termination with a negative result.

Fast free isolation searches movable freelists in reverse order within a preferred top quarter window and a wider top half fallback, uses a deeper scan at scan start and when no page is found, shortens the budget after finding a fallback candidate, isolates a chosen buddy block into the matching free list, and updates cached free positions and failure counters.

Fast free search holds the zone lock with interrupts saved while iterating movable freelists, reordering the list, and isolating the chosen block, releasing it before any surrounding pageblock isolation work.

Free isolation first attempts the fast path and returns if any free pages result; otherwise it scans pageblocks downward from the free cursor to the migrate cursor, yielding periodically, skipping offline ranges, applying target and recent failure suitability gates, using a stride that doubles on empty blocks and resets on success, and records the restart cursor.

The compaction allocation callback supplies a destination folio of matching order by splitting the smallest available larger isolated block, invoking free isolation at most once when empty, then applying allocation hooks, establishing a reference count, preparing compound metadata for larger orders, and debiting both free and migrate counters.

The compaction free callback returns a destination folio to the per order isolated free list only when its last reference is dropped and preparation succeeds, while unconditionally restoring the corresponding migrate page count.

Compound page preparation marks the first page as head, initializes each following page in the power of two range as a tail linked to that head, then completes head initialization for the given order.
Migration isolation reports one of three outcomes: abort scanning immediately, isolate nothing and continue scanning, or isolate pages and proceed to migration.
